A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same t-SNE study. Their main text, figures, equations, and complete Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments and t-SNE/PCA analyses of PBMC3k, credit-card fraud, and BBC news data, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical demonstrations and adds PCA preprocessing, poison-point robustness, and UMAP experiments in its appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1's impostor construction, the t-SNE objective, and the existing poison-point procedures are retained. The new poison-point theorem formalizes an existing attack; preprocessing and UMAP experiments do not revise the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 Figure 11 adds a controlled synthetic test contrasting the exactly equidistant X0 and two-block clustered X1 constructions under insertion of a shared center point. The real datasets and broader tasks remain unchanged; larger samples and PCA variations primarily change evaluation settings.

E2.justification: UMAP changes from cited background to an evaluated comparator across impostor, near-simplex, poison-point, and outlier experiments (v2 Appendices A.3 and B.2). PCA is removed from the corresponding single-cell impostor comparison, although retained in other experiments.

E3.justification: The single-cell comparison changes from DBSCAN labels derived from the t-SNE output to a partition from the input's Ward dendrogram. New protocols vary PCA preprocessing, dataset size, and injection counts, and explicitly test perplexity 1. The BBC outlier setting is also revised from alpha > 1 to alpha in (0.8, 1), despite retaining the plotted results; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of whether cluster exaggeration survives PCA preprocessing, whether single-point poisoning persists at larger sample sizes, and whether the constructed Theorem 7 example behaves as predicted (Figures 7–11). New UMAP analyses examine shared failure modes and differences in responses to poison points and outliers.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional plots do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial preprocessing, robustness, and UMAP results and removes v1 Table 1's three-index numerical comparison. Single-cell t-SNE silhouette scores change from 0.514/0.619 to 0.429/0.462 for original/impostor inputs, under changed clustering labels, so these are not comparable performance changes. The BBC t-SNE scores remain 0.399/0.196/0.418; new UMAP scores are 0.528/0.314/0.377.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 7 and its proof establishing identical poisoned loss landscapes for differently clustered inputs, supported by a new nearest-neighbor affinity lemma. It replaces Lemma 6's construction proof with a continuity argument and corrects the deformation formula. The outlier derivation changes substantially, replacing the stated 3 + o(1) bound with 3.266 + o_n(1); several statements also expand their stated perplexity domain to include endpoints.

C1.justification: The two central failure-mode contributions remain. V2 qualifies the abstract from 'cannot be reliably inferred' to 'cannot always be inferred' and frames the cluster contribution around strong versus weak distance separation. Its discussion adds a preliminary extension to other force-based visualization methods.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes weakened metric separation from preserved neighbor ordering, qualifying v1's 'unclustered impostor' interpretation. It replaces the poison-point distance-gap explanation with affinity redistribution and perplexity dependence. New qualifications explain that PCA preprocessing breaks exact additive invariance and that UMAP differs in poisoning sensitivity and outlier placement.

D1.justification: V2 documents the financial input's 30 dimensions, the revised Ward-based clustering, and construction details and projection dimensions for the new preprocessing experiments. Algorithm 1, the BBC injection recipe, and the supplied code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V1's assertion that additive invariance had not been studied is replaced by attribution to Lee and Verleysen (2011; 2014). V2 also credits Schubert and Gertz (2017) for empirical outlier observations and adds prior work on noise robustness. These changes substantively revise the positioning of central mechanisms, beyond the bibliographic update to the existing Snoeck work.

P1.justification: The overall six-section narrative remains. V2 rewrites the introductory illustration and poison-point explanation, consistently emphasizes cluster salience, and subdivides Section 4 into distinct input/output and instability cases. Much of the surrounding exposition is retained.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the introductory table and small illustrations with a three-scenario overview figure, redesigns the single-cell figure around distance matrices and dendrograms, and adds extensive preprocessing, robustness, and UMAP displays. Several original empirical figures are retained with renumbering and revised captions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the support and interpretation of the central conclusions: it corrects mathematical derivations, formally supports the poison-point example, tests common PCA preprocessing, and distinguishes weak distance separation from preserved neighbor ordering. Corrected attribution and UMAP comparisons improve scientific context. The outlier bound becomes weaker but better supported; Section 5's inconsistent approximation of 3.6 remains a limited defect alongside Theorem 9's 3.266.
